# Acknowledgments {.unnumbered}

This book grew from work and conversations across computer architecture,
machine-learning systems, and benchmarking. I am grateful to the students,
collaborators, colleagues, and members of the broader research community who
questioned its framing, challenged weak claims, and kept the argument grounded
in evidence. Their questions and examples repeatedly brought the discussion
back to what architects can measure, verify, and defend.

I am especially grateful to Parthasarathy (Partha) Ranganathan, Vice President
and Engineering Fellow at Google, who delivered the inaugural keynote at the
online Architecture 2.0 workshop. That workshop gave the effort its early
momentum and helped turn an emerging idea into a broader community
conversation.

Srivatsan Krishnan (Harvard) led the research project that generated many of the
ideas discussed in this book. I am particularly grateful for his contribution.

Many other colleagues helped test and sharpen the vision behind this book. I am
grateful to Saman Amarasinghe (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), David
Brooks (Harvard University), Dan Connors (NVIDIA), Siddharth Garg (New York
University), Brian Hirano (Micron), Qijing Jenny Huang (NVIDIA), Ravi Iyer

Tushar Krishna (Georgia Institute of Technology), Benjamin C. Lee (University

University), Yingyan (Celine) Lin (Georgia Institute of Technology), Jason

Divya Mahajan (Georgia Institute of Technology), Ankita Nayak (Qualcomm),
Phitchaya Mangpo Phothilimthana (Google DeepMind), Matt Sinclair (University of

The book is stronger because of their questions and contributions. Any errors

## Use of Generative AI {.unnumbered}

I used generative AI systems while developing this material to test outlines
and arguments, draft and revise prose, write and debug code, and check
consistency. The ideas, architectural judgments, selection and interpretation
of evidence, and final editorial decisions are mine. I reviewed the text,
sources, executable examples, and figures, and accept responsibility for the
material's accuracy, originality, and conclusions.
